## Generation over host-memory weights in pieces, now for every weight; a hand-set expert RAM tier capped to what is safe

- **On a discrete card, generation reads every weight kept in host memory in pieces.** 2026.11.27.01 split the one-token GEMV of such weights into launches of at most 4 MB each, so that no launch reads over PCIe for long (#99, an Arc A380's 4B hung at the first token after a 131K prompt). It split only the matrices loaded the usual way. The output head (the 4B's among them) and the stacked matrices still ran as one launch: Qwen's DeltaNet qkv + z, Gemma's weights and head, the drafters' heads, Inkling's stacks and the MoE router with the shared expert. Now they are split too. The start line that names the host-memory part also says how those GEMVs run. On the laptop's iGPU, with weights forced into host memory and 1 MB pieces, the 4B's and the 27B's results stayed the same bit for bit, and the head and the 27B's DeltaNet stack now ran in pieces. An iGPU's default is unchanged: one launch, since its host memory is its own RAM.
- **A hand-set `--expert-ram-gb` / `ARC_XRAM_GB` above what Windows lets the GPUs map is capped to it.** Before, it was only warned about, and such a tier could hang the GPUs or run out of memory (manoreken2: 47 GiB a GPU ran, 48 hung; PR #100). One start line names the size asked for and the size used. Below that limit the size you set is used as before. On Linux, a split model's hand-set tier keeps the automatic size's caps (32 GiB a GPU, 128 in all). This cap has not yet run on a discrete card: on the laptop we checked only that the results did not change. An integrated GPU now ignores a hand-set tier, since its GPU memory is the RAM already.
- **The automatic choice to read the expert file through the OS file cache (`ARC_XBUF`) is made on discrete cards only.** `ARC_XBUF=1` still forces it anywhere.
- **The Windows launcher recognizes the Arc 140T by its PCI device ID** (0x7D51 / 0x7DD1, Arrow Lake-H, which the Arc 130T shares) when Windows names it only "Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics", as the Linux launcher already did.
- **Smaller:** `ARC_GV_K4=0` now wins over `ARC_GV_SMALL=2`, and gate + up in one launch (`ARC_GEMV_GU=1`) leaves weights in host memory to the split path.

**Please test on your machine** (paste the output into the issue):

- **#99, an Arc A380 or another card with little memory, at a 131K context:** the run that hung before, on this release:
  ```
  ./bin/runz <path>/Qwen3.5-4B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --bench-pp 131072 --n 1 --must-fit 2>&1 | tail -20
  ```
  The start line naming the weights in host memory should end with "their one-token GEMVs in pieces of at most 4 MB". If it resets again, add `sudo dmesg | grep -i -E "i915|xe |GPU HANG|reset" | tail -10`.
- **A hand-set expert RAM tier on discrete cards** (PR #100): the runs asked for in [this comment](https://github.com/rizagp/inferzero/pull/100#issuecomment-7208146950) and [this one](https://github.com/rizagp/inferzero/pull/100#issuecomment-7212096683).
